problem: Existing 3D referential grounding datasets (ReferIt3D, ScanRefer, SceneVerse) are limited in scale or naturalness, assume the referred object always exists, and offer no scene graphs, free-space references or imperfect statements. Models therefore cannot detect non-existent referents or suggest alternatives.
motivation: Real-world human instructions are often ambiguous or wrong (e.g. 'the remote on the table' when it is on the sofa), and robots need to detect this and interact to clarify. 3D vision-language data is scarce compared with 2D data, so a large, structured benchmark with imperfect language is needed.
key_idea: Build IRef-VLA, a large synthetic-language 3D benchmark (scene graphs, free-space annotations, minimal view-independent statements and imperfect statements about non-existent objects) and define referential grounding with imperfect references (detect non-existence and suggest alternatives).
insight: Training on IRef-VLA statements from ScanNet alone gives reasonable zero-shot transfer to Sr3D/Nr3D, and adding more scenes further helps 3D-VisTA (Nr3D 41.8 to 44.9, above SceneVerse zero-shot text 43.1). Scene-graph search with LLM parsing detects non-existence much better than a classifier head added to MVT (TP 90.4 vs 66.2), showing that structured scene-graph knowledge gives a useful upper bound for robust grounding.
method: Data sources: combines ScanNet, Matterport3D, HM3D, 3RScan, ARKitScenes and Unity scenes into 7,635 scenes / 11.5K regions / 286K objects (477 classes) with point clouds, object classes, boxes and dominant colours
Free-space annotation: horizontally traversable free space is extracted and split into sub-regions with spatial relations, so areas can be referenced ('the space near the table')
Scene graph generation: 8 heuristic relation types (above, below, closest, farthest, between, near, in, on) computed from yawed bounding boxes, giving 7.6M relations
Language generation: templates with synonyms produce 4.7M view-independent, unambiguous, minimal statements
Imperfect statements: one target/anchor attribute is altered to a similar value so the statement describes a non-existent object
Augmented MVT baseline: two-layer MLP binary existence classifier on concatenated object features, with grounding loss applied only for existing objects

Graph-search baseline: gpt-4o-mini few-shot (5 examples) parses statements into a subgraph; BFS+DFS searches the scene graph; if no exact match, partial-match statements are shown to the LLM in an MCQA prompt to choose an alternative

setting.backbone: MVT and 3D-VisTA (trained on IRef-VLA); MVT + binary head; gpt-4o-mini (frozen, few-shot) + graph search
setting.training_data: IRef-VLA (ScanNet subset or full; 80/20 train/val for non-ScanNet scenes; official ReferIt3D splits for ScanNet); graph search is training-free apart from few-shot prompts
setting.observation: 3D scene point clouds with object annotations / scene graphs (text statements)
setting.action_space: none (object grounding / existence classification / alternative selection, no navigation actions)
setting.privileged: Graph-search uses ground-truth heuristically generated scene graphs as knowledge base

results: 3D-VisTA trained on IRef-VLA-Full reaches 65.8% Sr3D and 44.9% Nr3D zero-shot, 1.8 points above SceneVerse zero-shot text (43.1%), and 60.6% on IRef-VLA Full. The graph-search baseline gets F1 94.4 for object existence vs 78.3 for MVT+classifier, and 61% alternative similarity.
limitations: Synthetic template language lacks view-dependent and allocentric statements
Heuristic alternative-similarity score does not capture human preferences
Single-turn only; no multi-turn dialogue or actual navigation; graph search relies on GT scene graphs
